name: Frozen French Fries

frozen.note: Single layer; shake once or twice for even crisping.

tips: No need to thaw or add oil.
Don't overcrowd the basket — cook in batches for crispier fries.
summary: Crispy frozen fries straight from the freezer, no oil needed.

name: Frozen Chicken Nuggets
tips: Shake or flip halfway.
Add 1–2 minutes for extra-crispy.
summary: Hot, crunchy nuggets in about 10 minutes.

name: Frozen Chicken Wings

frozen.note: Flip and separate halfway; go longer for extra-crispy.

tips: Pat dry after they thaw in the basket to crisp the skin.
Sauce after cooking, not before.
summary: Crispy wings from frozen — no thawing required.

name: Frozen Mozzarella Sticks

frozen.note: Flip once; watch closely so the cheese doesn't burst.

tips: Don't overcook — the cheese leaks out.
Leave space between each stick.
summary: Golden mozzarella sticks without the deep fryer.

name: Frozen Breaded Fish Fillets
tips: No oil needed for breaded fillets.
Single layer, no overlap.
summary: Crispy breaded fish fillets from frozen.

name: Frozen Fish Sticks
tips: Shake or flip halfway for even browning.
summary: Kid-favorite fish sticks, crisp in under 10 minutes.

name: Frozen Tater Tots
tips: Shake halfway.
Single layer gives the crispiest tots.
summary: Extra-crispy tots without deep frying.

name: Frozen Onion Rings
tips: Arrange in a single layer so they crisp evenly.
summary: Crunchy onion rings from the freezer.

name: Frozen Spring Rolls
tips: A light spritz of oil boosts crispiness.
summary: Crispy spring rolls, no deep frying.

name: Frozen Egg Rolls
tips: Spritz with oil for a golden shell.
summary: Restaurant-style egg rolls from frozen.

name: Frozen Shrimp

frozen.note: Cook straight from frozen; smaller shrimp need less time.

doneness.label: Shellfish — cook until 145°F / opaque and curled

tips: Toss raw shrimp with a little oil and seasoning first.
Pre-cooked shrimp only need reheating — check at 4–5 minutes.
summary: Plump shrimp in minutes, from frozen.

name: Frozen Pizza Rolls
tips: Let them cool a minute — the filling gets molten.
summary: Crispy pizza rolls in well under 10 minutes.

name: Frozen Meatballs

frozen.note: Most frozen meatballs are pre-cooked — you're reheating through.

tips: Shake halfway.
Toss in sauce after air frying.
summary: Hot, browned meatballs ready for sauce or subs.

name: Frozen Hash Brown Patties
tips: Single layer, no overlap, for crisp edges.
summary: Crispy diner-style hash brown patties.

name: Frozen Dumplings & Potstickers

frozen.note: Spritz with oil first for crisp bottoms.

tips: Shake halfway.
Serve straight away while the wrappers are crisp.
summary: Crispy-bottomed dumplings without a pan.

name: Frozen Corn Dogs

frozen.note: Flip halfway; mini corn dogs need 6–8 minutes.

tips: No oil needed.
summary: Fair-style corn dogs at home.

name: Frozen Burrito

frozen.note: Flip halfway; unwrap any plastic first.

tips: Wrap in foil for a softer shell, or leave bare for crispy.
summary: A crispy-shelled burrito, heated right through.

name: Frozen Broccoli

frozen.note: No need to thaw; shake for even roasting.

tips: Toss with oil after it thaws in the basket for crispier florets.
summary: Roasty frozen broccoli, crisp at the edges.

name: Frozen Chicken Tenders
tips: Single layer for the crispiest coating.
summary: Crunchy chicken tenders straight from frozen.

name: Frozen Sweet Potato Fries

frozen.note: Shake often — they brown fast at the tips.

tips: Single layer prevents sogginess.
summary: Sweet, crisp fries from the freezer.

name: Chicken Breast

fresh.note: Flip halfway; time depends heavily on thickness.

tips: Pound to an even thickness so it cooks evenly.
Rub with a little oil and seasoning first.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
summary: Juicy chicken breast — always cook to 165°F at the thickest part.

name: Boneless Chicken Thighs

fresh.note: Flip halfway.

doneness.label: Poultry — cook until 165°F (thighs are great up to 175°F)

tips: Skin-side down first, then flip to crisp.
Thighs are forgiving — hard to dry out.
summary: Juicy, crisp-edged thighs in about 20 minutes.

name: Bone-In Chicken Thighs

fresh.note: Skin-side up; flip once.

doneness.label: Poultry — cook until 165°F at the bone

tips: Pat dry and oil the skin for maximum crunch.
Check temperature next to (not touching) the bone.
summary: Crispy-skinned bone-in thighs.

name: Chicken Wings

fresh.note: Toss every ~8 minutes; bump to 400°F for the last few minutes to crisp.

tips: Pat very dry and toss with a little baking powder for extra crunch.
Sauce after cooking.
summary: Crackly wings without a drop of frying oil.

name: Chicken Drumsticks

fresh.note: Turn halfway.

tips: Oil and season the skin well.
Turn once for even color.
summary: Crispy drumsticks the whole table will grab.

name: Chicken Tenders (Fresh)

fresh.note: Flip halfway.

tips: Bread them for crunch, or go plain for a quick protein.
summary: Homemade tenders, crisp outside and juicy in.

name: Whole Chicken

fresh.note: Roughly 6 minutes per pound; start breast-down, flip halfway. Depends on size and air fryer.

doneness.label: Poultry — 165°F in the breast, 175°F in the thigh

tips: Use a thermometer — size makes time vary a lot.
Make sure the bird fits with room for air to circulate.
Rest 10 minutes before carving.
summary: A whole roast chicken with shatteringly crisp skin — thermometer essential.

name: Hamburgers

fresh.note: Flip halfway; time varies with thickness and desired doneness.

tips: Add cheese in the last minute.
Ground beef must reach 160°F — don't serve burgers rare from an air fryer.
summary: Juicy burgers in under 15 minutes — cook ground beef to 160°F.

name: Steak

fresh.note: Flip halfway; time depends on thickness and doneness. Use a thermometer.

doneness.label: Beef — USDA safe is 145°F + 3-min rest (medium-rare ~130–135°F is a personal-risk choice)

tips: Pat dry and oil for a good sear.
Pull a few degrees early and rest 3–5 minutes — carryover keeps cooking.
summary: A quick weeknight steak — target your doneness by temperature, not time.

name: Beef Meatballs (Fresh)
tips: Make them even-sized so they finish together.
summary: Browned, juicy meatballs for pasta or subs.

name: Steak Bites

fresh.note: Shake halfway; smaller cubes cook faster.

tips: Single layer so they sear instead of steam.
summary: Fast, seared steak bites for bowls and salads.

name: Pork Chops

fresh.note: Flip halfway; thicker bone-in chops need longer.

tips: A light oil rub and seasoning is all they need.
Rest 3 minutes so they stay juicy.
summary: Tender pork chops — 145°F and a short rest is the target.

name: Bacon

fresh.note: No preheat; check often. Thick-cut needs longer. Lower temp reduces smoking.

tips: Empty the grease tray between batches to avoid smoke.
Cook in a single layer; strips can overlap slightly.
summary: Crispy bacon with less mess — mind the smoke from the drippings.

name: Sausages

fresh.note: Turn halfway; thin breakfast links need less.

tips: Prick nothing — they stay juicier whole.
Turn once for even browning.
summary: Browned, blistered sausages in about 12 minutes.

name: Bratwurst

fresh.note: Turn halfway.

tips: Great with peppers and onions tossed in for the last 6 minutes.
summary: Juicy brats with a snappy skin.

name: Pork Tenderloin

fresh.note: Turn once; time varies with thickness.

tips: Sear-brown outside, blush-pink center at 145°F is perfect.
Rest before slicing.
summary: A tender pork roast in about 20 minutes.

name: Salmon

fresh.note: Skin-side down; no need to flip. Thicker fillets need longer.

tips: Oil the basket or use a liner so the skin doesn't stick.
It keeps cooking after you pull it — stop at flaky.
summary: Flaky salmon with a lightly crisp top in under 10 minutes.

name: Shrimp (Fresh)

fresh.note: Shake halfway; they cook fast, so check early.

tips: Toss with oil and seasoning first.
Overcooked shrimp turn rubbery — pull them at opaque.
summary: Sweet, snappy shrimp in well under 10 minutes.

name: White Fish Fillet (Fresh)

fresh.note: Flip gently halfway if thick.

tips: Oil lightly so it doesn't dry out.
Bread or batter for a fish-and-chips feel.
summary: Flaky white fish, plain or breaded.

name: Scallops

fresh.note: Flip halfway; they cook very quickly.

tips: Pat very dry for a better sear.
Don't overcook — they turn tough fast.
summary: Restaurant-style scallops in minutes.

name: Salmon (From Frozen)

frozen.note: Cook a few minutes to thaw, then season and finish.

tips: Season once the surface thaws enough to hold it.
Thicker fillets need the top of the range.
summary: Weeknight salmon with no thawing ahead.

name: Broccoli

fresh.note: Shake once; spritz with water if the tips brown too fast.

tips: Toss with oil, salt and a little garlic.
Don't overcrowd or it steams instead of roasting.
summary: Charred-tip, crisp-tender broccoli in about 10 minutes.

name: Brussels Sprouts

fresh.note: Halve them; shake halfway. Cut-side crisps up beautifully.

tips: Toss with oil and a pinch of salt.
A drizzle of balsamic after cooking is excellent.
summary: Caramelized, crispy sprouts — a converter for skeptics.

name: Asparagus

fresh.note: Thin spears cook faster — check at 6 minutes.

tips: Snap off the woody ends first.
Finish with lemon and parmesan.
summary: Tender-crisp asparagus in under 10 minutes.

name: Cauliflower
tips: Toss with oil and spices — it loves bold seasoning.
Great as buffalo cauliflower with sauce added after.
summary: Golden, roasty cauliflower with crisp edges.

name: Baby Potatoes

fresh.note: Halve larger ones; shake once or twice.

tips: Toss with oil, salt and rosemary.
Test with a fork — they should pierce easily.
summary: Crispy-outside, fluffy-inside little potatoes.

name: Potato Wedges

fresh.note: Soak cut wedges in water 15 min, then dry, for extra crispiness.

tips: Single layer; shake halfway.
Season after cooking so the salt sticks.
summary: Steak-house wedges without the fryer.

name: Baked Potato

fresh.note: Flip once; large potatoes need the top of the range.

tips: Prick all over, rub with oil and salt for crackly skin.
Squeeze-test: it should give when done.
summary: A fluffy baked potato with the crispiest skin you've had.

name: Sweet Potato (Whole)

fresh.note: Flip once; size drives the time.

tips: Prick the skin first.
Done when a knife slides in with no resistance.
summary: Caramel-soft baked sweet potato.

name: Zucchini

fresh.note: Slice into rounds or spears; it releases water, so don't crowd.

tips: Pat dry after salting to avoid sogginess.
Parmesan added late crisps into a crust.
summary: Roasty zucchini that isn't watery.

name: Green Beans
tips: Toss with oil, garlic and a squeeze of lemon.
They should blister but stay snappy.
summary: Blistered, garlicky green beans in minutes.

name: Mushrooms

fresh.note: They shrink and release water — shake to help it evaporate.

tips: Toss with oil, garlic and thyme.
Don't wash them soggy — brush clean.
summary: Deeply browned, meaty mushrooms.

name: Carrots

fresh.note: Cut into even sticks; thicker pieces need longer.

tips: A little honey in the last few minutes makes them glaze.
summary: Sweet, tender-crisp roasted carrots.

name: Corn on the Cob

fresh.note: Turn halfway; cut cobs to fit the basket.

tips: Rub with oil before, butter after.
Look for lightly charred kernels.
summary: Charred, sweet corn without boiling a pot.

name: Tofu

fresh.note: Use firm/extra-firm; shake for all-over crisp.

tips: Press out water 15 minutes, then toss with oil and cornstarch for maximum crunch.
Season or sauce after cooking.
summary: Golden, crunchy tofu cubes — the cornstarch trick is key.

name: Kale Chips

fresh.note: Low and quick — watch closely, they burn in seconds once dry.

tips: Dry the leaves well, use just a little oil.
Salt lightly right after.
summary: Shatter-crisp kale chips — keep an eye on them.

name: Roasted Chickpeas

fresh.note: Dry them very well first; shake a couple of times.

tips: Season after cooking so spices don't burn.
They crisp more as they cool.
summary: Crunchy, snackable chickpeas.

name: Reheat Pizza

fresh.note: Reheating leftovers — heat through and re-crisp the base.

tips: The base goes crisp again — far better than a microwave.
Add fresh toppings for the last minute.
summary: Leftover pizza with a crispy base, like new.

name: Hard 'Boiled' Eggs

fresh.note: No water needed; 15 min for soft-set yolks, 17 for firm. Then plunge into ice water.

tips: Times vary by air fryer — dial in your first batch.
Ice-bath immediately for easy peeling.
summary: Hands-off 'hard boiled' eggs with no pot of water.

name: Toast

fresh.note: Flip halfway; check early, it browns fast.

tips: Great for a slice or two when the toaster's busy.
summary: Quick toast without a toaster.
